title: Effective gluing of sheaves of sets on localized sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $U$ an object and $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ a covering family indexed by a set. Work in a universe containing the site, $I$, all section sets and their indexed products [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $U_{ij}=U_i\times_UU_j$ and $U_{ijk}=U_i\times_UU_j\times_UU_k$. Give each slice $\mathcal C/V$ the localized topology, and use restriction along the slice functors [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Suppose $F_i$ is a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C/U_i$ for each $i$, and $\phi_{ij}:F_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j|_{U_{ij}}$ are isomorphisms for all pairs, including equal indices. Assume $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$ after restriction to $\mathcal C/U_{ijk}$ for every triple. Then there are a sheaf of sets $F$ on $\mathcal C/U$ and isomorphisms $e_i:F|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i$ such that $\phi_{ij}\circ e_i|_{U_{ij}}=e_j|_{U_{ij}}$ for every pair.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves (with the gluing datum immediately preceding it)

proof.text: The site axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)(iii) gives $U_i\times_UV$ for every $V\to U$, since $U_i\to U$ belongs to the given covering. Apply it with $V=U_j$ and then $V=U_j\times_UU_k$ to obtain all double and triple overlaps in the statement. For $W\to U$ put $W_i=W\times_UU_i$ and $W_{ij}=W\times_UU_i\times_UU_j$. The family $\{W_i\to W\}$ is a covering, and base changing it along $W_j\to W$ gives $W_{ij}$ and a covering of $W_j$. All maps between these objects below are induced by their projections and the pullback universal property. The localized coverings and restrictions are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: On $\mathcal C/U$ define $H_i(W)=F_i(W_i\to U_i)$ and $K_{ij}(W)=F_j(W_{ij}\to U_j)$, with restriction maps induced by pullbacks. For any covering $\{W_\lambda\to W\}$, its base changes cover $W_i$ and $W_{ij}$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)(iii), applied once and twice. The pullback universal property identifies their double intersections with $(W_\lambda\times_WW_\mu)_i$ and $(W_\lambda\times_WW_\mu)_{ij}$. Thus the sheaf equalizer axioms for $F_i$ and $F_j$ on these coverings are exactly the sheaf equalizer axioms for $H_i$ and $K_{ij}$. They are sheaves.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: The transition isomorphisms give two natural maps $\prod_iH_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}K_{ij}$ whose $(i,j)$ coordinates on a tuple $x$ are $\phi_{ij}(x_i|_{W_{ij}})$ and $x_j|_{W_{ij}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise](1), applied on the small site $\mathcal C/U$, their products and equalizer are sheaves computed sectionwise. All index categories (discrete $I$, discrete $I\times I$, and the finite parallel-pair category) and section products lie in the stipulated universe. We obtain a sheaf $F$ with $F(W)=\{(x_i)\in\prod_iF_i(W_i):\phi_{ij}(x_i|_{W_{ij}})=x_j|_{W_{ij}}\text{ for every }i,j\}$. Its restrictions are coordinatewise; naturality of $\phi_{ij}$ preserves these equations, and the functor laws follow from those of the $F_i$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: Pull the cocycle for $(i,i,i)$ back along the triple diagonal $U_i\to U_i\times_UU_i\times_UU_i$. For $\alpha_i=\Delta_i^*\phi_{ii}$ it gives $\alpha_i=\alpha_i\circ\alpha_i$. Since $\alpha_i$ is an automorphism, cancellation gives $\alpha_i=\mathrm{id}_{F_i}$. This is diagonal normalization; no assertion that $\phi_{ii}$ is identity on the whole self-overlap is needed.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: For $W\to U_i$, let $d_i:W\to W_i$ be the graph of its structural map and define $e_{i,W}(x)=d_i^*x_i$. Given $y\in F_i(W)$, define a tuple $b_{i,W}(y)$ by $x_j=\phi_{ij,W_j}(y|_{W_j})$, where $W_j\to U_i\times_UU_j$ uses the structural map through $W\to U_i$ and the projection to $U_j$. On $W_{jk}$ the cocycle pulled back along $W_{jk}\to U_i\times_UU_j\times_UU_k$ gives $\phi_{jk}(x_j|)=\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}(y|)=\phi_{ik}(y|)=x_k|$. Thus this tuple belongs to $F(W)$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: The composite $e_{i,W}b_{i,W}(y)$ equals $y$: its formula is $\phi_{ii}$ restricted along $W\to U_i\times_UU_i$ with both coordinates the structural map, so Step 4 applies. For $x\in F(W)$, pull its $(i,j)$ compatibility equation back along $W_j\to W_{ij}$ whose $i$ coordinate is induced by $W\to U_i$ and whose $j$ coordinate is the projection. This gives $x_j=\phi_{ij}((d_i^*x_i)|_{W_j})$, the $j$ coordinate of $b_{i,W}e_{i,W}(x)$. Both composites are therefore identities.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: For $h:W'\to W$ over $U_i$, let $h_j:W'_j\to W_j$ be its base change. The graph identity $h_i\circ d'_i=d_i\circ h$ gives $e_{i,W'}(h^*x)=(d'_i)^*h_i^*x_i=h^*d_i^*x_i=h^*e_{i,W}(x)$. Naturality of $\phi_{ij}$ gives $h_j^*\phi_{ij,W_j}(y|_{W_j})=\phi_{ij,W'_j}((h^*y)|_{W'_j})$, so the $j$ coordinates of $h^*b_{i,W}(y)$ and $b_{i,W'}(h^*y)$ agree. Consequently $e_i$ and $b_i$ are natural inverse maps, giving $e_i:F|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, compatible-tuples construction and its omitted verifications

proof.text: For a test object $W\to U_i\times_UU_j$ and $x\in F(W)$, pull its $(i,j)$ compatibility equation back along the graph $W\to W_{ij}$ of the two structural maps. Naturality of $\phi_{ij}$ identifies the resulting equation with $\phi_{ij,W}(d_i^*x_i)=d_j^*x_j$. These are $\phi_{ij,W}(e_{i,W}(x))$ and $e_{j,W}(x)$. Equality for every test object and section is the required equation $\phi_{ij}\circ e_i=e_j$ on the double slice.

split_report.summary: Second reading restored the original general-site statement: the site axiom supplies every required overlap pullback. Expanded the compatible-tuples construction, component sheaf verification, sectionwise-limit construction, diagonal normalization, graph inverse, both inverse equations, naturality and overlap compatibility. No new nodes; the existing descent node assumes all fibre products and cannot be applied to the general site of this item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-0297e2c3c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole item, the four cited nodes' statements, Stacks sites.tex:5826-5880 (the glueing-data paragraph and lemma-glue-sheaves, Tag 04TR) and Definition 00VH at :679. The statement matches 04TR one hypothesis at a time: a general site, a covering, sheaves of sets F_i on C/U_i, isomorphisms phi_ij for all pairs including equal indices, the triple cocycle, and the conclusion phi_ij e_i = e_j. Removing the first reader's 'all fibre products' hypothesis is correct: 00VH(iii) builds the double and triple overlaps from the covering, and the second reader's x->u<-y example confirms the extra hypothesis is strictly stronger. Steps 1-8 are correct on my own check. Step 2's component sheaves need only base change plus (i)+(ii) for the isomorphic families. Step 3 is the equalizer of products, using clause (1) of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise on the site C/U with small index categories. Step 4's diagonal normalization pulls the (i,i,i) cocycle back along the triple diagonal and never claims phi_ii=id on all of U_ii. Steps 5-8 cover membership of the inverse via naturality and the pulled-back cocycle, both composites through W_j->W_ij, naturality, and overlap compatibility through the graph W->W_ij. Edge cases checked: empty cover, singleton identity cover, empty section sets, non-monomorphic U_i->U. Duplicates: lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent assumes all fibre products, so its existence clause is a special case of this item and not a restatement; the maintainer may later make it cite this item. The module-gluing nodes do not specialize to sets. Mathlib has IsStack only as an assumed instance (Descent/IsStack.lean:57-80), so 'no match' holds, and all three search kinds are recorded. The blueprint place det-pe-torsor-comparison-glue proof paragraph 2 ('Étale sheaves glue along Zariski coverings', proof.md:18) is verified. The route is clean: only definitions and a Mathlib leaf, tool_uses empty, no SGA. There are no new nodes and no fixes.
